Hi Nina — thanks for the invoice. I99m Rafael from Finance; copied Laura for customer record. I99ve attached bank_details_v2.pdf with the accounts we maintain. Summary and recommendation below.

1) Preferred instruction (general)
- For USD receipts we prefer OUR where available (sender covers all intermediary/correspondent charges). That ensures the full invoice amount posts.
- Where OUR is not available (some INR rails), use SHA but request your bank to add the FT reference/invoice number in the MT103/MT202. That allows us to trace deductions quickly.

2) EUR / GBP / USD accounts
- EUR: IBAN: DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00 (Deutsche Bank, SWIFT DEUTDEFFXXX). Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Ltd.
- USD: Account: 0012345678, ABA: 021000021 (Wells Fargo, SWIFT: WFBIUS6S). Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Inc.
- GBP: Sort code: 20-30-40, Account: 55667788 (Barclays, SWIFT: BARCGB22).

3) INR / local-rupee collections (to avoid correspondent bank fees)
- We do have a local INR collection account in India (ICICI Bank, Mumbai). Account details are included in the attached PDF. Using the INR local account eliminates most correspondent deductions. If your bank supports sending to that account domestically, please choose that flow.

4) Correspondent / intermediary banks
- For some USD->INR flows, the routing uses Standard Chartered London as an intermediary. If your bank uses a US-USD intermediary, intermediary fees can still be deducted on the chain.

5) Fee handling options and reconciliation
- Option A (preferred): Instruct "OUR" so the beneficiary receives the invoiced amount. If "OUR" is unavailable, instruct SHA and include full MT103 details; we will accept net-of-fees but we require: (a) full remittance advice from your bank with deduction details; (b) an on-file shortfall reconciliation request within 7 business days.
- Option B (operational simplicity): Send to the local currency collection account if available (EUR/INR), which avoids most intermediaries.

6) Goodwill credit policy
- Finance can approve a one-time goodwill credit up to $150 USD for captured intermediary deductions on a case-by-case basis (requires remittance evidence). For persistent deduction patterns we99ll ask the customer to change routing method.

Please include the invoice number in the payment reference (INV-98721). If you decide to proceed with USD OUR but your bank says OUR is unsupported for INR, let us know and we99ll apply the local INR account flow.

Thanks,
